headline: High: Notion AI can ingest shared workspace content while caveman can write project files, creating default-path prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can write files like CLAUDE.md and project notes, while Notion AI reads workspace pages and databases. That creates a plausible shared-content bridge where attacker-controlled text in workspace content or notes can influence downstream prompting. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly observed, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF caveman writes instructions into shared project notes or CLAUDE.md that Notion AI later reads
IF Notion AI is asked to summarize or answer from workspace pages containing adversarial text
mitigations: Separate prompt-instruction files from shared workspace content
Add a review step before Notion AI consumes caveman-authored notes
Prefix untrusted text with explicit non-instruction markers
Restrict caveman writes to a dedicated folder
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between file writers and Notion AI readers

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch workspace-like content: caveman handles session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Notion AI accesses workspace pages and databases under the user's Notion permissions. If those notes contain sensitive material, Notion AI can surface it through vendor backends. The shared-data pathway is documented enough to support medium severity.
conditions: IF caveman stores secrets or sensitive project notes in files that are also synced into Notion workspace content
IF Notion AI is used on pages containing confidential data
mitigations: Move secrets out of shared notes immediately
Limit Notion AI use to non-sensitive pages
Redact sensitive fields before summarization
Audit workspace pages for copied logs or memory files
requires-engineering: enforce data-class labels and access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and writes files, but Notion AI is vendor-hosted and explicitly has no host execution, shell, or filesystem write. The pair therefore lacks the overlapping write-to-same-resource pattern needed for a stronger conflict finding. Any conflict would require unusual workspace setup, so low fits better than medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace files through an external sync layer
IF caveman writes files that Notion AI also edits through Notion-controlled actions
mitigations: Avoid concurrent edits to the same document
Use separate workspaces for drafting and knowledge base content
Lock shared pages during review
Keep caveman outputs read-only in Notion
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency or locking across the sync boundary

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so it may treat caveman-authored notes as authoritative input. caveman can generate project notes and CLAUDE.md content that then becomes source material for Notion AI summaries or answers. That creates a default-path cascade from generated text into downstream reasoning, though Notion AI still has some grounding.
conditions: IF caveman-generated notes are imported into Notion pages
IF Notion AI is used to summarize or answer from those imported notes without human verification
mitigations: Mark caveman output as draft-only
Require human review before importing into Notion
Ask Notion AI for citations to source pages
Cross-check important claims against original sources
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Notion AI processes workspace pages through vendor backends and downstream model providers. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into Notion, residency and retention obligations may differ from local project files. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data from caveman files is copied into Notion workspace pages
IF the workspace contains data subject to retention or residency rules
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion AI workflows
Review Notion retention settings before use
Store compliance-sensitive notes in a separate system
Minimize copied logs and memory files
requires-engineering: map data classes to residency and retention controls
